messages:
kai: Heads-up — seeing a cluster of latency escalations across hosted text-gen after last runtime build (commit abc123). Multiple customers report p95 jump from ~180ms -> ~420ms and p99 from ~300ms -> ~950ms on gpt-small-8k route. All traces point to attention kernel step ballooning. Suspect FlashAttention/SDPA kernel selection regression. :eyes:

sana: Filed CASE-5521 with support details and a reproducible curl. Customer repro: steady stream of 1-2k token requests. Repro commands below. Logged their trace IDs: trace/ci-99102, trace/ci-99103. I can attach logs if needed.

sana: ```
# minimal repro
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"gpt-small-8k","input":"hello world"}'
```

oliver: I profiled a canary instance with --profile-run against a 2k token request. Timeline: total rose from 160ms -> 480ms. Breakdown shows attention kernel time went 3-5x higher. Kernel selection log: "selected=flash_attn_v2 compiled_with=AVX512 target=ampere". On some hosts runtime attempted flash_attn but hit a slow microkernel (likely a codegen/compile flag mismatch). SDPA path is still faster on those hosts.

oliver: Here is a snippet from the runtime kernel selection log:```
[2026-02-28T14:12:03Z] model=gpt-small-8k seq=2048 selected_kernel=flash_attn_v2 compile_flags="-O3 -march=skylake-avx512" fallback=sdp_enabled=false
```

maria: Proposed mitigations: short-term -> flip runtime flag to prefer sdpa for affected routes; rollback the abc123 kernel compiler flags; enable canary to 5% then 20% then 100%. Long-term -> add more robust kernel ABI/os checks and a runtime microbenchmark at startup to choose the fastest kernel per host.

cheng: Quick hotfix config we pushed to canary (example):
```
{
  "model_routes": {
    "gpt-small-8k": {
      "kernel_overrides": {"attn_impl": "sdpa"},
      "notes": "hotfix-1745678901"
    }
  }
}
```

oliver: I rolled a patch to the runtime: `--feature enable_flash_attn=false` for the canary pool and forced attn_impl=sdpa. Command used: `redwood-runtime patch --pool canary --set attn_impl=sdpa --annotation "hotfix latency regression"`.

deploy-bot: Starting rollout for config hotfix:hotfix-1745678901 -> canary (5% nodes).

maria: Monitoring metrics now. Initial canary at 5% shows p95 back to ~200ms, p99 ~340ms. Looks promising. Increasing to 20% in 10m. :thumbsup:

oliver: Notes from profiling the patched canary: attention kernel times returned to baseline. No increase in CPU or memory. Kernel selection now logs `selected=sdpa` on the previously impacted hosts.

maria: After 20% and smoke checks, we promoted to 100% production. Post-rollout aggregate: p95 ~190ms, p99 ~320ms for gpt-small-8k. Customer CASE-5521 contacted and updated.

sana: Customer confirmed improved latency on their side after ~25min. Marked the case as mitigated and added follow-up for permanent fix.

oliver: Root cause hypothesis: the compiler flags merged in abc123 caused a codegen variant for flash_attn_v2 that performs poorly on certain GPU driver/hw combos (kernel micro-op scheduling/regression). The runtime's kernel selection favored flash_attn over sdpa due to a missing microbenchmark step after new binaries.

maria: Action items: 
- oliver: open PR to add runtime microbenchmark and ABI check (small kernel perf on startup) to detect best attn_impl per host.
- eng-ml: revert/patch the compile flags used in abc123 and re-run CI perf suite across GPU matrix.
- devex: add a feature-flagging playbook for toggling attn_impl per-route + runbook for support.
- support: follow up with customers and update CASE-5521 notes.

oliver: PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2418 (adds microbenchmark + opt-in env var REDWOOD_FORCE_ATTN_IMPL).

maria: I'll prep a retro and postmortem after we validate CI matrix. For now the hotfix stands. Thanks everyone.

support-bot: CASE-5521 -> status: mitigated, updated: 1745679320, assignee: sana.

kai: Nice work. Please make sure the canary logs and kernel-selection traces are centrally archived and searchable (link to our internal trace index). We should also add an alert on sudden p95/p99 delta > 2x for any model route. :+1:
